EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a strong C=O stretch at 1700 cm⁻¹, diagnostic of an aldehyde conjugated to an aromatic ring. The intense 1592 cm⁻¹ band matches an aromatic C=C stretching mode. Two medium-strong bands at 632 cm⁻¹ and 703 cm⁻¹ are typical for aryl C–Cl stretches (Nakamoto GFQ-046, GFQ-041), implying more than one C–Cl bond. The 843 cm⁻¹ band fits an out-of-plane C–H/Cl deformation of 1,2,4-substituted benzenes, while bands at 1159, 1213, 1095 and 1083 cm⁻¹ correspond to in-plane C–H and C–Cl vibrations of chlorobenzenes. Aldehydic C–H stretch appears at 2870 cm⁻¹ and aromatic C–H stretch at 3073 cm⁻¹, both present. No strong ~1345 cm⁻¹ band characteristic of NO₂ symmetric stretching is observed, arguing against nitro-containing candidate 9. Overall the pattern best fits 2,4-dichlorobenzaldehyde (candidate 1: O=Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1Cl).
